{{further|2026 China Open (tennis)}}

[[Zheng Qinwen]] defeated [[Mirra Andreeva]] in the final, 7–5, 6–4 to win the women's singles tennis title at the [[2026 China Open (tennis)|2026 China Open]]. It was her first [[WTA 1000]] title, sixth [[WTA Tour]] title overall, and first title in [[2024 Toray Pan Pacific Open – Singles|over two years]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4590546/zheng-qinwen-makes-history-with-china-open-wta-1000-title|title=Zheng Qinwen makes history with China Open WTA 1000 title|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=11 October 2026}}</ref> Zheng became the first Chinese player and first wildcard to win the [[China Open (tennis)|China Open]]. She was also the second Chinese player to reach the women's singles final, after [[Chen Li (tennis)|Chen Li]] in [[1996 Nokia Open – Singles|1996]].

[[Amanda Anisimova]] was the reigning champion,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20251005-us-open-finalist-anisimova-beats-noskova-to-win-beijing-title|title=US Open finalist Anisimova beats Noskova to win Beijing title|date=5 October 2025 |publisher=France 24|accessdate=5 October 2025}}</ref> but she withdrew before the tournament due to a wrist injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4581969/jessica-pegula-defending-champion-amanda-anisimova-withdraw-from-china-open-with-injuries|title=Pegula, defending champion Anisimova pull out of China Open with injuries|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=25 September 2026}}</ref>

This marked the first tournament played by [[Elena Rybakina]] as the incumbent [[List of WTA number 1 ranked singles tennis players|world No. 1]]. With her second-round defeat to [[Alina Charaeva]], Rybakina became the second player (since the introduction of the [[WTA rankings]]) to lose their first match played as world No. 1, after [[Naomi Osaka]] at the [[2019 Dubai Tennis Championships – Women's singles|2019 Dubai Tennis Championships]]. Ranked No. 118, Charaeva became the lowest-ranked player to defeat an incumbent world No. 1 from a set down at a WTA Tour event since the rankings began in 1975.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4586105/charaeva-upsets-new-world-no-1-rybakina-in-beijing-second-round|title=Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=3 October 2026}}</ref>
